title: Bacon and Egg Pie
subtitle: A New Zealand-style shortcrust pie with streaky bacon and whole baked eggs
excerpt: Rashers of streaky bacon and whole eggs set in a shortcrust case, baked until the whites are just firm and the yolks are still a little soft. Simple to assemble and travels well for picnics.
sourceNotes: The bacon and egg pie is a New Zealand institution; this version follows the classic approach with whole eggs rather than beaten egg.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best eaten the day it is baked, either warm or at room temperature. Keeps in the fridge for one day.

content.text: The appeal of this pie is in its plainness: bacon, eggs, pastry. The eggs go in whole so each slice reveals a cross-section of set white and a yolk that runs a little if the timing is right. Rest the pie well before cutting, or the egg whites will slip around.

items.prepNote: two thirds for the base, one third for the lid
5 for the filling, 1 beaten to glaze

content.text: Cook the streaky bacon in the frying pan over a medium heat until just starting to colour but not crispy. It will continue cooking in the oven. Remove and drain on a plate. Leave to cool.
Heat the oven to 200C. Roll out two thirds of the pastry and line a 23cm pie dish, leaving a 2cm overhang. Chill for 15 minutes.
Lay half the bacon over the base of the pastry case, overlapping the rashers slightly. Scatter over the spring onion and parsley if using.
Break the 5 eggs carefully over the bacon, spacing them evenly across the pie. Season generously with black pepper. Lay the remaining bacon over the top of the eggs.

Roll out the remaining pastry for a lid. Brush the rim with beaten egg. Lay the lid on and press firmly to seal. Trim and crimp the edges, then brush the top with beaten egg. Cut a small slit in the centre.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the pastry is deep golden. The egg whites should be set; insert a skewer to check if you are unsure.
Rest for at least 15 minutes before slicing. The pie is also very good at room temperature.

items.symptom: The egg whites are still runny after baking.
items.cause: The oven was not hot enough, or the pie was sliced too soon.
items.fix: Return the pie to the oven for a further 5 minutes and rest for the full 15 minutes before cutting.

items.symptom: The base is pale and doughy.
items.cause: The pie was not baked on a hot surface.
items.fix: Preheat a heavy baking tray in the oven and bake the pie on it to give the base heat from below.

items.cause: The pie was cut while still hot.
items.fix: Rest for at least 15 minutes, or allow to cool fully and slice cold.
